headline: High-risk shared filesystem and write-capable pair create prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error exposure by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor ingests workspace files, open editor buffers, clipboard, and MCP outputs; semantica reads local files, web pages, email, streams, and MCP resources. Because both can exchange content through shared files/MCP, attacker-controlled text from one can be treated as instructions by the other. This is documented in both profiles, though not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF Cursor opens semantica-produced files or MCP resources as trusted instructions
IF semantica ingests Cursor-written workspace content without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following from file/MCP content
Separate workspaces and MCP endpoints per agent
Add provenance labels to all exchanged artifacts
Review any cross-agent text before execution

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, clipboard contents, and can egress broadly to model providers; semantica touches enterprise data, contracts, audit trails, and can read many file and API sources. If they share a workspace or clipboard, sensitive data can flow from semantica into Cursor’s third-party inference path, creating a realistic exfiltration risk in default use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or clipboard
IF Cursor sends semantica-derived content to external model providers
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent
Disable clipboard sharing between agents
Route sensitive semantica data through redacted copies only
Restrict Cursor to local-only or approved-provider mode
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention on shared files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, and use MCP. Cursor’s per-window sessions share state via the local filesystem, while semantica uses a single shared intelligence layer. Concurrent writes to the same repo or graph-backed artifacts can race and corrupt state without locking.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or directory
IF git operations occur without an external lock or merge gate
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize git writes with a manual lock
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files
Use separate branches per agent
requires-engineering: add filesystem locking around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor can generate code or file edits that semantica may ingest as structured inputs, and semantica is designed around provenance, decision records, and deterministic graph construction. If semantica treats Cursor output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into downstream records, commits, or actions without a verification step.
conditions: IF semantica consumes Cursor-produced files or records as trusted inputs
IF no human or automated verification step checks Cursor output before semantica acts
mitigations: Require explicit validation before import
Mark Cursor outputs as untrusted by default
Compare outputs against source data before action
Limit semantica to read-only review mode for Cursor artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance-based gating

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor is a closed-source editor with broad network egress and model-provider calls, while semantica handles enterprise data, contracts, audit trails, and secrets. If regulated or confidential data from semantica reaches Cursor’s external providers, the pair can create a compliance breach. The profiles do not show a residency or DPA safeguard, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF semantica data includes regulated or contractual records
IF Cursor forwards that data to external model providers without an approved DPA or residency control
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Cursor sessions
Use redacted or synthetic copies
Restrict external model calls for sensitive projects
Document residency and retention requirements
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing
